rules.heading: Spells
rules.text: Spells are the strange, dangerous, and occasionally irresponsible way crawlers bend reality. Some Spells heal wounds or reshape the battlefield, and others exist primarily to make something stop moving— permanently. Spells cannot be attempted untrained except via a scroll. Every Spell listed in this section follows the same core rules for things like casting, targeting, and spend-ing Mana. Spell listings include a variety of terms or fields associated with them, including: Name: The name of the Spell appears as a headline to the entry. Type: Whether the Spell is an Attack or Passive is noted under the flavor text. The type of damage delivered from Attack Spells is also listed here for quick reference. Spells default to your Int Mod for to-hit and damage rolls. If a different Stat is listed here, that Stat is used to hit and damage, but Spells all still use Intelligence for Mana. If the spell is Favored by any particular Classes, other Classes pay 1 additional Mana to cast it. Mana Cost: The Mana cost to cast the Spell. Range: The range of the Spell. Melee means 5ft (adjacent). Duration: Some Spells are not instantaneous. When the duration is reached, the Spell effect wears off at the end of that round. AI Favor: Low-damage Spells grant AI Favor to you if you use such a wimpy attack for a majority of your attacks during a combat that lasts for at least three rounds. Limitations: If there are conditions, requirements, or exclusions, they go here. Cooldown: If the Spell has a cooldown, it is listed here. You can’t cast the Spell during its cooldown. Description: Any notes or descriptions of the general effect seen when you cast the Spell are listed here. If the Spell requires a Spell Check, that is also provided here. Base Damage: This is the damage the Spell deals with 1–4 Ranks in the Spell. You add your Int to the base damage, unless it says otherwise. The damage type is listed here as well. Upgrades: These are bonuses you gain when you reach the listed Rank in the Spell. The first entry of each benefit adds a damage die of the same type to the base damage of the Spell. Additional damage dice and effects are also listed here.

rules.heading: Spells in Your Hotlist
rules.text: Don’t forget that Spells need to be in your Hotlist to cast them in combat or other stressful situations. Write down the specific combat text for your Spell in the “Attacks” section on the front of your character sheet. When you write a Spell on your Hotlist, you need only list additional notes like the Mana cost and Range of the Spell. Attack Spells require you to make an Attack Skill Check vs. the target’s Evade. Spells that don’t require a Check to be made when cast (non-Attack Spells) are tagged as Passive and simply happen, but those are not marked for Skill Advancement (p. 169) when used. Instead, their Ranks must be raised via magical means or trained at a guild.

rules.heading: Creating Your Own Spells
rules.text: In the ways that count, Spells are just a special type of Skill. Create them in the same way as you’re create a Skill (p. 174–175).

spells.name: Air Buddy
spells.flavor_text: “There’s no dungeon rule that a dog can’t fly.”
spells.description: You launch yourself with enough force to fly, hurtling forward from your current position up to 10 × your Int Mod away. You land safely if you land on solid ground; otherwise, you fall (see p. 76). You can cast this twice in a row to “double jump” just like in platforming video games.

upgrades.5: You may choose one additional willing target up to your size at touch range, who you bring with you.
upgrades.10: You can fly up to 20 × your Int Mod away with this spell.
upgrades.15: You may choose up to five additional willing targets up to your size at touch range to bring with you.

spells.name: Astral Paw (Astral Hand, Astral Claw)
spells.flavor_text: “You have summoned an Astral Paw. Yes, just the paw. Budget constraints.”
spells.duration: Until the end of combat or 5 minutes.
spells.description: You conjure a spectral hand, paw, or claw, looking much like your own. You can use this astral appendage to manipulate objects up to 30ft away by spending an Action. You can use the Astral Paw to make Skill Checks but suffer Disadvantage due to a lack of fine control.

upgrades.5: Your Pugilism and Slice Attacks with the Paw add 1 Astral Paw Rank damage die.
upgrades.10: You can conjure a paw up to four size categories larger than your own, and the range increases to 50 feet.
upgrades.15: The caster no longer suffers Disadvantage when performing suitable Skill Checks using the paw, and the duration is 15 minutes.

spells.name: Confusing Fog
spells.flavor_text: “Visibility reduced. Decision-making questionable.”
spells.duration: Until the end of two full rounds of combat or 20 seconds
spells.description:
You create a billowing cloud of fog that you, your party members, and friendly NPCs can see through, but it obscures the area from Mobs, making it more difficult for them to attack you. Mobs attack with Disadvantage (see Mob Advantage and Disadvantage, p. 60) against targets in the fog.

This fog fills a 25 × 25ft area. Smart Mobs may attempt to move the combat out of the fog if able.

upgrades.5: The fog fills a 50 × 50ft area, and its duration is 1 minute.
upgrades.10: The fog fills a 100 × 100ft area and lasts for 5 minutes.
upgrades.15: The fog fills a 500 × 500ft area and lasts for 15 minutes.

spells.name: Grand Illusion
spells.flavor_text: “Why, yes, that is my pet T-Rex.”
spells.description:
You create an illusion that might trick your foes. Make a single Int-Opposed Spell Check vs. foes who can see it. Your same roll is used against foes who see it even after the casting round.

Mundane illusions seeking only to impress might be rolled with Advantage, while complex illusions seeking a specific response or images that suddenly pop up during combat might be rolled with Disadvantage (GM’s discretion).

On Success, they believe your illusion.

upgrades.5: Those who believe gain the Woozy Debuff or similar based on the desired response.
upgrades.10: Those who believe also gain the Queasy Debuff or similar based on the desired response.
upgrades.15: Those who believe also gain the Shocked Debuff or similar based on the desired response.

spells.description: You create a magical orb of light that follows slightly above and behind you. It provides bright light for a 20ft radius and dim light for a 20ft radius past that.

upgrades.5: You can move the orb up to 20 feet away from you.
upgrades.10: You can move the orb up to 60 feet away from you and can double the radius of the brightness with a thought.
upgrades.15: You can move the orb up to 100 feet away from you and attach it to a surface as an Action.

spells.name: Turn Undead
spells.flavor_text: “What is dead should stay dead… and far away.”
spells.tags_raw: Attack, Area of Effect, Favored: Bard, Cleric, & Paladin
spells.description:
Make a single Cha-Opposed Spell Check vs. the Undead Mobs in the affected area.

On Success, the Undead Mob runs away for the duration of the Spell.

upgrades.5: +5ft Cone. Duration is 5 rounds.
upgrades.10: +10ft Cone. Duration is 10 rounds.
upgrades.15: +15ft Cone. Duration is 15 rounds. On an Amazing Success or better, the Undead Mob is destroyed.

spells.name: Wilbur’s Slow-Build Fireblast
spells.flavor_text: “Hold. Hold! HOLD!”
spells.base_damage: 1d8 + Int Fire, and the target gains the Burned Debuff.
spells.description:
This Spell can be cast and held as a swirling ring of fire around your ring finger until you unleash it. Only one ring may be held at a time. The next time you perform an Attack Action, it must be this Spell (at no additional Mana cost).

If anyone touches the ring with the intent to diffuse it (you may oppose that Action), the Attack hits them for half damage. The appendage they touched you with smolders, useless for a number of rounds equal to the damage inflicted.

upgrades.5: +1d8 base damage. For each full day you hold the spell, +1d8 Fire damage.
upgrades.10: +1d8 base damage and +5ft Splash.
upgrades.15: +1d8 base damage and +5ft Splash.
